brief.subject: FTC pulls 19 fake FTC websites as imposter scams persist
brief.headline: FTC takes down 19 sites posing as the agency, flags health plan marketers
brief.dek: Imposter scams remain a top fraud threat, and open enrollment brings FTC warnings to 25 health plan marketers and lead generators.
brief.lede: The FTC says it has removed 19 websites pretending to be the FTC itself. Its imposter crackdown has also produced more than $80 million in consumer redress since 2024.

sections.heading: Fake FTC sites taken down
bullets: 19 websites impersonating the FTC have been removed, a reminder that scammers copy even fraud-fighting agencies.
Enforcement under the FTC's Impersonation Rule has yielded more than $80 million in consumer redress since the rule took effect in 2024.
The FTC calls imposter scams the top reported fraud category, so treat any unexpected 'government' contact with suspicion.
Real agencies won't pressure you to pay quickly; hang up and look up the official contact yourself.

sections.heading: Open enrollment: watch health plan pitches
bullets: The FTC sent warning letters to 25 companies that market health plans or sell sales leads for them.
The letters flag likely deceptive or unfair claims about plan terms, a risk while families shop during open enrollment.
More letters are coming on a rolling basis, signaling the agency sees an ongoing problem.
Before signing up, confirm in writing what a plan actually covers, not just what a caller promises.

sections.heading: 'Risk-free' cancellation that wasn't
bullets: Riverside Payments Inc. and affiliate Cascade Equipment Leasing LLC will pay $600,000 over FTC and Washington state allegations.
Officials say the firms falsely promised savings and made 'risk-free' cancellation nearly impossible for small businesses.
Separately, the FTC and several states sued Toast Inc., alleging hidden fees and deceptive subscription and cancellation practices.
If a parent runs a small shop, review processing contracts for cancellation terms and unexpected fees.

brief.seo_description: FTC removes 19 fake FTC websites, warns 25 health plan marketers during open enrollment, and settles over 'risk-free' cancellation claims.
